chunks: A group of scholars informed us from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Sufyan al-Bazufari from Ahmad ibn Idris from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Hisham ibn Ahmar from Salima, the maidservant of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I was present with Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) when death approached him and he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he said: 'Give al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (who is al-Aftas) seventy dinars, and give so-and-so such and such, and so-and-so such and such.'

I asked: 'Do you give money to one who attacked you with the blade, intending to kill you?' He replied: 'Do you want me not to be among those about whom Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, said: "And those who join that which Allah has bidden to be joined and have awe of their Lord and fear the evil reckoning."' Yes, O Salima, indeed Allah, the Exalted, created Paradise, purified it and purified its fragrance. And its fragrance is found from a journey of two thousand years, but those who are disowned by parents and those who cut off family ties will not smell its fragrance.

key_terms.الْأَفْطَس: Al-Aftas (a specific epithet/name for al-Hasan ibn Ali)
key_terms.وَالَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ: And those who join that which Allah has bidden to be joined (Quranic quote)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of giving to those who attack you according to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s) magnanimity by bestowing wealth upon his cousin al-Afṭas, who had stabbed him, thereby embodying the Quranic ideal of maintaining ties commanded by Allah. The Imam explicitly links this ethical conduct to the fragrance of Paradise, noting that those who sever kinship bonds are excluded from its scent, a key motif in Shia eschatology regarding the Mahdi's lineage. This narrative serves to refute claims that the Imamate ended with al-Sadiq by demonstrating the continuity of his noble character and divine connection.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 161 - Informed us a group of scholars from Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Sufyan Bazufari from Ahmad bin Idris Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Isa from Hasan bin Mahbub from Jamil bin Salih from Hisham bin Ahmar from Salima, maidservant of Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that she said:

I was present at the time of the passing away of Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) when the Imam was in a swoon in his last moments. After that he regained his consciousness and gave seventy dinars to Hasan bin Ali bin Husain – or the same Hasan Aftas – to give such and such amount to so and so person and such and such amount to so and so person.

I asked: Would you give money to one who attacked you and wanted to slay you? He replied: Don’t you want me to be one, about whom Almighty Allah has said: “And those who join that which Allah has bidden to be joined and have awe of their Lord and fear the evil reckoning.” [13:21] Yes, O Salima, Allah, the Mighty and Sublime has created Paradise and purified and made it fragrant in such a way that the fragrance of Paradise reaches upto a distance of two thousand years’ of travel, but it will not reach to those who are disowned by parents and those who cut off relationships.
